decisionBox.changed: Everything changed. Midnight published a range read with a bullish tilt, a 78,674.8 reduce gate and a 79,025.8 add gate, and inside four hours the add gate fired, the second-stage 79,244.8 filter cleared, and price ran 1,731.6 points off the 78,791.9 entry to 80,523.5. The bias moves from range to bullish. The decision box moves from ADD to TAKE_PROFIT - not because the structure broke but because open interest FELL 1.63 percent while price rose 0.83 percent, which makes this a short-covering squeeze rather than a new-money bid, and because 1,081.2 points of the move have already been handed back. Both gates are re-anchored inside 0.4 hourly ATRs of spot so that whichever one resolves first, it resolves inside this session.

liquidityMagnet.note: Called BALANCED on purpose, and the two halves of the evidence disagree, which is the finding. The cumulative record is overwhelmingly one-sided: 13,194,932 USD of short-side liquidations against 1,584,393 USD long-side, an 8.33-to-1 skew, and that whole ladder from 79,000 up to 80,500 has been consumed in the last four hours. A spent ladder pulls nothing, and above 80,523.5 there is no mapped fuel at all. Against that, the newest 14 minutes of flow is long-side at 79,250. So the up-magnet is history and the down-magnet is live, but the down-magnet is small. Neither side has enough forced fuel left to drag price on its own - the next move has to come from real bids or real offers.

liquidations.note: The single most important number in this report is that open interest FELL. It reads 2,221,974,797 USD against 2,258,817,141 at midnight, down 36.8m or 1.63 percent, while price rose 0.83 percent. Price up on falling open interest is short covering - positions being closed, not opened. The liquidation record confirms it: 13,194,932 USD of short-side liquidations against 1,584,393 USD long-side over the trailing 20.6 hours, an 8.33-to-1 skew, with the heaviest damage at 80,250 and 79,500. `skew` is reported as the OKX retail long/short ACCOUNT ratio (ccy=BTC, period=1H), newest print 11:00Z, at 1.04. That is DOWN from 1.12 at midnight and it fell in a straight line through the rally - 1.12, 1.10, 1.06, 1.05, 1.05, 1.04. Retail accounts got less long as price went up, which is the opposite of the usual chase and removes the crowding risk midnight was worried about. Funding is 0.00511 percent per 8h, essentially flat, so nobody is paying up to hold this. Net read: the rally was fuelled by shorts covering into an empty book, retail did not join, and the fuel is now spent.

earnings.note: The 26 August print landed well - TipRanks summarised the session as 'Nvidia Blasts Past Earnings Estimates' - and the read-through is visible in the ETF rather than in crypto. QQQ closed 711.37, up only 0.09 percent, and is quoted 716.82 in pre-market at 07:50 EDT, up 0.77 percent. BTC's own reaction over the same window was the 1,731-point squeeze, but that squeeze started at 08:00Z, roughly twelve hours after the print, and coincided with falling open interest - so attributing it to NVDA would be a stretch this desk is not making.

The same TipRanks recap flagged PCE inflation coming in hot on Wednesday, and the rates market agrees: the US 10-year is 4.66 percent, essentially flat on the 4.664 prior close, and the dollar index is 99.201, up 0.04 percent. Neither moved on the BTC squeeze, which is another sign the move was internal to crypto positioning rather than a macro repricing.

calibration.note: Midnight's ADD gate FIRED and paid, and it is the second consecutive session where an add gate has been collected. It required a settled 1H close above 79,025.8: the 07:00Z bar closed 79,079.1, clearing the line by 53.3 points, and the very next bar ran to 80,025.9 and closed 79,763.4. Midnight's second-stage filter at 79,244.8 cleared on the same impulse. Midnight's REDUCE gate at a settled close below 78,674.8 did NOT fire; the lowest 1H close since publication is 78,828.0 and the lowest print is 78,753.0, some 78.2 points above the line - so the decision to re-anchor that gate from the EMA20 down to the EMA50 was correct, because a gate left at 78,718.3 would have been wicked. Midnight deployed 12 USDT into the spot core at 78,791.9 and spot is 79,442.3, so the tranche is up 0.83 percent, roughly 0.10 USDT. acting_helped is TRUE. The transferable finding is about gate SIZING, not placement. Midnight wrote its add gate 233.9 points out, 0.58 hourly ATRs, and explicitly called that 'deliberately just outside the half-ATR trigger band' - and it fired anyway, within four hours. That is the first gate outside the band to fire, and the reason is that the ATR itself was wrong: 405.07 was the tightest reading of the week, a coil measurement, and the release expanded it 27 percent to 515.94. Measured against the POST-break ATR, midnight's gate was 0.45 ATRs out - inside the band after all. The amendment: when ATR has contracted three sessions running, it is understating the distance a break will cover, and gates should be placed against a normalised ATR rather than the compressed one.
